news.name: AI Tools Amplify Skills, Not Replace Them in Coding and Creativity
news.summary: Conversations highlight how using AI to enhance thinking sets people apart from those just generating basic content. In coding, engineers note AI struggles with efficient, performant code despite handling simple tasks well, while creative fields see it as a workflow booster that frees humans for originality and emotion. Throughout, the consensus emerges that AI multiplies intelligence for skilled users but risks average outcomes without strong human input and oversight.

news.name: Debate Heats Up Over Whether AI Writes Better Code Than Humans
news.summary: Engineer Arpit Bhayani sparked the discussion on October 25, declaring no human will ever code better than large language models, a view echoed by many who say the debate is settled and it's time to move on. Critics like programmer Valentin Ignatev counter that AI spots bugs but delivers shallow fixes without rethinking architecture, while others note humans still lead in complex reasoning and novel problems. The exchange highlights a field in transition, where developers shift from raw coding to guiding AI on design, verification, and oversight.

news.name: AI Uncovers Software Bugs Too Fast for Patches, Warn CEOs
news.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman warned at Stanford that AI finds bugs beyond normal hacker reach, like hardware-level issues, making patching obsolete and pushing for AI-driven defenses. Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince noted millions of exploit attempts hit newly disclosed PHP vulnerabilities affecting 70% of PHP sites, including WordPress and firewalls, patched October 21, 2026. Economist Noah Smith fears this could turn the free internet into a costly guarded space, though some say AI aids fixes and mass exploits haven't surged as feared.

news.name: Developers Debate AI's Role in Easing Game Coding Drudgery
news.summary: A discussion highlights that 90% of game coding involves tough, repetitive tasks like fighting compilers and fixing bugs, while AI tools could handle that load to free humans for imagination and decisions. Builders note AI already speeds up scripts, data generation, and routine fixes, though understanding and maintaining the code remains key. While some worry AI might eventually touch creative work, most see it as a helpful collaborator that cuts toil without replacing human judgment.

news.name: Over 1,000 Mathematicians Form Group to Reject Commercial AI in Research
news.summary: The Association for Human Mathematics, formed earlier this year, now has 1,008 members who commit to avoiding technical help for commercial AI firms and publishing only their own writing. Of those, 654 in the AI-free caucus abstain from AI entirely in core tasks like finding proofs or posing questions. The move responds to AI companies like OpenAI releasing generated manuscripts, sparking debate: supporters value human insight like chess engines aiding understanding without replacing it, while critics call it resistance to progress.

news.name: Engineer Claims LLMs Outcode Humans Forever
news.summary: On October 25, Arpit Bhayani posted that LLMs have surpassed humans at writing code, urging everyone to accept it and move on. Some agreed, pointing to AI's speed and clean outputs in studies like those on GPT-4, while others highlighted gaps in performance, reliability, and senior-level judgment on tradeoffs and system health. The exchange underscores how developers see AI as a fast tool for iteration that still needs human expertise to guide and refine.

news.name: Developers Wishlist New Language for AI Agents
news.summary: Pocock called for a language with Bend as an early promising example, sparking replies from hundreds of developers who stressed compilers as essential error-catchers for agent-written code. Chris Lattner promoted Mojo for its advanced types and hardware support, while others pushed for introspectable designs like Elixir and debated hurdles for new languages. The conversation shows developers rethinking language priorities around speed, safety, and agent-driven coding realities.

news.name: Rethinking AI Prompts for Bigger Ambitions
news.summary: A conversation highlights moving beyond faster task completion with AI toward loftier goals, inspired by Mollick's call to amp up ambition and Felix Rieseberg's framework of speed, altitude, depth, and range. Rieseberg's tutorial breaks it down—for example, depth means prompting AI like a top professional using raw data and real methods, while range pulls in outside perspectives like psychology or journalism. Users are testing these in workflows, refactoring codebases and spotting overlooked issues, with the key lesson that under-asking limits what models can achieve as they advance.

news.name: Private Equity Report Questions AI's Broader Economic Gains
news.summary: Apollo Global Management's chief economist Torsten Slok released a report on October 24 showing revenue per worker and profit margins rising only for the Magnificent 7, while flat for the other 493 S&P 500 companies. Most firms outside tech view AI token spending as a cost center rather than a growth driver, limiting macroeconomic effects. Gartner warns of a $4.9 trillion revenue gap for data-center spending by 2030, raising impairment risks for over $3.5 trillion in infrastructure, as discussions note potential hiring slowdowns and early semiconductor weakness.

news.name: AI Coding Agents Create Divide Between Old and New Startups
news.summary: Conversations highlight how startups built manually over the past three years feel outpaced by those launched this year with agent-written code, leading some to rebuild entirely for faster iteration and fewer backlogs. Jake Gold predicts even top AI firms like OpenAI could soon seem like 'pre-AI legacy' companies, urging pre-product-market-fit teams to consider re-founding. While studies show AI boosts code output by 30 percent and more, quality reviews and customer demands slow incumbents, though deep user knowledge offers them an edge. Richard Artoul noted that nothing slows progress like paying customers who can't be disrupted.

zh.title: Grok Bot 是什么
bullets: 三层架构：Jarvis（云端主控 Bot）→ Vision（Linux 云主机）→ Friday（本地 Mac 工作站）
DN-B 编排：Driver = dsh / deepseek-flash（effort max）；Navigator = Codex CLI gpt-6-astra（长流程 -p max）
审代码优先 Codex CLI（档位 ≥ 编程任务），Paseo 审查代理兜底
内置 X 公开读：搜帖 / 用户帖 / 新闻 / 趋势（无需自备开发者密钥）

en.title: What is Grok Bot
bullets: Three layers: Jarvis (cloud chief bot) → Vision (Linux cloud host) → Friday (local Mac workstation)
DN-B: Driver = dsh / deepseek-flash (effort max); Navigator = Codex CLI gpt-6-astra (long flows -p max)
Code review prefers Codex CLI (effort ≥ coding task); Paseo reviewer as fallback
Built-in X public reads: search posts / user posts / news / trends (no personal developer key required)
